chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Nawfali, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he disliked eating meat with the animal (i.e., consuming the meat while the animal's body is still present or attached).

key_terms.بِالْحَيَوَانِ: With the animal (referring to the living or recently slaughtered animal's body)
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (expressing a recommended dislike, not prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to dislike eating meat with the animal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic preference (karahah) against consuming meat directly from the living or freshly slaughtered animal while it is still attached, emphasizing ritual purity and proper preparation. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the animal's essence and its consumable parts, ensuring the meat is properly detached and prepared according to fiqh guidelines.
